notes:
Summary: SpryBridge builds millisecond-sensitive personalization and chat features inside a consumer ecommerce app. Very latency + cost sensitive — mobile first. Team wants Redwood to prove cost/perf delta on production-like traffic.

Key quotes / snippets: 
- 'We need P95 < 80ms for user-facing personalization flows (including network hop) — 95th important for retention.' 
- 'If quantization gets us 2x lower cost with <5% quality hit we'll move to dedicated.'

Technical requirements & preferences: 
- Workload: real-time personalization + lightweight chat support + reranking for recommendations.
- Target SLOs: P50 ~30ms, P95 <=80ms end-to-end for 512-token-ish exchanges (mostly short prompts).
- Throughput target: 350-500 req/s peak for US region; burst to 1k during promos.
- Latency sensitivity: high; cost sensitivity: high (aim to reduce per-token by 40-60%).
- Model preferences: open Llama-like variants + custom fine-tuned reranker. Evaluate quantized 4-bit and 8-bit profiles.
- Routing/fallback: prefer canary -> dedicated -> hosted fallback; want automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant when capacity constrained.

Optimize interest (explicit asks): batching/caching strategy recommendations; suggested cache TTLs for personalization prefixes; quantization profiles to benchmark (4-bit, nf4, int8-ish); guidance on kernel/runtime tradeoffs; a benchmark harness run vs their local fp16 baseline.

Security/compliance: must run inside VPC with SSO/SAML and KMS integration; audit logs retained 12 months initially. Data residency: US only for payment-linked PII.

POC scope proposed: 
- Redwood runs performance matrix: (fp16 on A100) vs (4-bit quantized on A100) vs (nv-fp16 on T4/A10) with batching tuned (1-8) and KV-cache enabled.
- Measure token throughput, P50/P95 latencies, cost per 1M tokens, and quality delta on internal eval set (prompt pairs).
- Deliver routing config for canary + automatic fallback and batching presets.
